title: PHOTO RELEASE: “Josh on the Job” — Gottheimer Visits Magpie Bakery in Bloomingdale
text:
Above: Gottheimer with staff at Magpie Bakery.

BLOOMINGDALE, NJ — Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) visited Magpie Bakery in Bloomingdale to meet with local owners and employees, working with their team and hearing first-hand from Jersey customers as part of his “Josh on the Job” series highlighting locally owned small businesses and franchises across northern New Jersey.

“Small businesses like Magpie Bakery are the backbone of our economy and the heart of our communities,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “They’re up before dawn every morning serving Jersey families, and they deserve a partner in Washington who’s fighting to lower costs, cut red tape, and help them grow. I had a great time getting behind the counter with this team, and I’ll keep showing up to hear directly from the workers, owners, and customers who keep Bloomingdale running.”

During his visit, Gottheimer joined staff behind the counter, speaking with employees and customers from across the community about the challenges and opportunities facing small businesses today.

Gottheimer regularly visits small businesses and franchises across New Jersey’s Fifth District as part of his Josh on the Job series to hear directly from workers, owners, and customers about the issues impacting their jobs and their communities.

title: RELEASE: Gottheimer Joins Darren Drake Foundation, Drake Family for Darren Drake Memorial
text:
Above: Gottheimer at Darren Drake Memorial.

NEW MILFORD, NJ — Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) joined the Darren Drake Foundation and the Drake family at New Milford High School for a special memorial flag-raising ceremony to commemorate the life of Darren Drake and highlight Gottheimer’s bipartisan Darren Drake Act, which was signed into law to help combat lone-wolf terror attacks.

Watch Gottheimer’s full remarks here.

“It’s hard to believe that it’s been nine years since New Milford and the Drakes lost Darren. A blink of an eye. Yet, as we promised then, we would always honor Darren’s memory. This community has never forgotten,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “The Darren Drake Act has become an essential tool in our arsenal to eradicate terrorist threats in our country. And, it exists because of Jimmy and Barbara – and Darren.”

Gottheimer’s bipartisan Darren Drake Act, signed into law in December 2022, helps stop terrorists from easily acquiring trucks and other vehicles to use as weapons in attacks. Working closely with vehicle rental companies and in consultation with federal, state, and local law enforcement, the legislation requires the U.S. Department of Homeland Security to take concrete steps to stop known terrorists from renting vehicles.

On October 31, 2017, Darren was murdered in a terrorist attack while on a New York City bike path, where he was deliberately run down by an ISIS sympathizer in a rented pickup truck. The Darren Drake Foundation was created to honor his legacy and pursue the ideals and vision he was so passionate about.

Gottheimer was joined by Mayor Michael Putrino, Councilman Matthew Seymour, and Councilman Arthur Zeilner.

title: RELEASE: Gottheimer Joins North Jersey Families Helped With Military Pension Back Pay, Health Insurance Coverage, IRS Refunds, and More
text:
Above: Gottheimer joins Jersey constituents.

HACKENSACK, NJ — U.S. Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) joined North Jersey constituents, including veterans, seniors, nurses, and local families, to discuss how his office helped them receive benefits and services they were owed from federal agencies and private companies. Their cases included military pension back pay, health insurance coverage, identity theft, immigration paperwork, and delayed IRS refunds.

Gottheimer’s full remarks can be found here.

“One of the most important parts of my job is being an advocate and a champion for the families I’m lucky to represent here in North Jersey. By fighting for our Fifth District families, we’ve helped thousands of residents who’ve been denied Social Security checks, unemployment benefits, VA benefits, critical health care, tax refunds, or crucial resources they need, often because of bureaucratic red tape,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “Whether it’s the IRS, an insurance company, or a federal agency that’s gotten it wrong, I’ll always fight for Jersey families across the Fifth District to get what they are owed and deserve. If you need help with any issues, including Medicare, Social Security, passports, VA benefits, and so much more, please reach out to me.”

In the last five years alone, Gottheimer’s office has helped more than 780 veterans access their VA benefits and service medals; more than 1,834 Fifth District seniors access their earned Social Security checks and claw back over $2.6 million from the Social Security Administration; get more than 65 constituents back home from being trapped overseas, including some stranded in Israel after October 7; more than 4,500 constituents get their unemployment benefits; and claw back over $120 million owed to small businesses, non-profits, and constituents from the IRS. In total, Gottheimer’s office has clawed back more than $173 million to date for constituents through its casework team. Just among the cases highlighted today, the office helped get back more than $171,000 for Fifth District families.

Gottheimer joined Fifth District residents today:

Tom Gallagher of Mahwah: Tom’s brother, Retired Air Force Major John P. Gallagher, served in the U.S. Air Force for over 20 years and now lives in an assisted living facility after being diagnosed with early dementia. Tom holds power of attorney and looks out for him. For five months, Retired Major John’s pension was not being deposited because his bank account had been closed due to fraudulent and unauthorized withdrawals. Tom reached out to Gottheimer’s office for help working with the Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS), and Gottheimer’s team got right to work and contacted DFAS. The next day, DFAS processed John’s forms and placed his pension account back in active pay status. Within a week, DFAS confirmed the issue was resolved and that his brother’s back pay had been issued. In less than two weeks, Tom confirmed that his brother’s owed pension had received the gross pay he earned after waiting for five months.

Suzanne Jackson of Highland Lakes: Suzanne is a registered nurse who has spent more than 40 years caring for patients at Englewood Hospital. This past July, she reached out to Gottheimer’s office after UnitedHealthcare denied coverage for a prosthetic limb, initially deeming it not medically necessary. Although her doctor said she qualified for a K3 prosthetic with a microprocessor knee, UnitedHealthcare only approved a K2 prosthetic after her first appeal, which meant she could not continue working 12-hour shifts as a nurse. After months of fighting the decision, and being unable to reach anyone at UnitedHealthcare to escalate her appeal, Suzanne turned to Gottheimer. His team contacted UnitedHealthcare and asked them to take another look. Just a day later, UnitedHealthcare approved the K3 prosthetic with a microprocessor knee, and Suzanne is still on the job at Englewood Hospital.

Joey Shimm of Tenafly, on behalf of his wife, Yoko: Yoko’s green card arrived with a typo, an extra initial in her name, and the replacement came back with the very same mistake. When Yoko’s 95-year-old mother suffered a cerebral hemorrhage in Japan, Yoko needed a USCIS-approved travel document to get to her side, and the earliest appointment USCIS would offer was after her planned flight. Joey turned to Gottheimer’s office. His team immediately contacted the USCIS Newark Field Office Congressional Lead and secured an appointment for the very next day. Yoko received an ADIT stamp in her Japanese passport, which provides temporary proof of her lawful permanent resident status, and she traveled to Japan to be with her hospitalized mother. Gottheimer’s office will keep working with the family until the green card itself is fully corrected.

Robert Lunzer of Englewood: For a year, money had been coming out of Robert’s monthly Social Security retirement benefit, and he had no idea why. It turned out to be from missing payments on a more than $93,000 Small Business Administration (SBA) COVID loan he never took out. The application didn’t even have his real name on it, only a signature he never signed, and the money was going to an offshore bank account. After two weeks of getting nowhere with the SBA, Robert called Gottheimer’s office. His team contacted the SBA the very next day, and the inquiry was sent to the SBA’s fraud unit. In just one week, the SBA validated Robert’s identity theft claim, forgave the entire $93,600 fraudulent debt, stopped the garnishment of his Social Security benefits, and refunded about $4,500 to him in a lump sum.

Ann Marie and Jim Dunlop of Haworth: Ann Marie and Jim, both in their eighties, filed their taxes in mid-March, on time. The IRS told them to complete an ID verification over the phone, and then they never heard another word, aside from a letter every six weeks saying the IRS needed more time. Gottheimer’s team contacted the Taxpayer Advocate Service (TAS), learned that the return was under review because of unverifiable income and withholding, and worked with Ann Marie and her accountant to gather the records needed to verify her withholding. Gottheimer’s office got the documents to TAS, a referral then went to the IRS, and in just a few short weeks, the Dunlops’ refund of more than $22,500 was in the mail.

Kevin Noah of Vernon: Kevin filed his federal tax return, and eight months went by without a word from the IRS. When the agency finally asked for additional documentation, it was documentation he could no longer get his hands on. Kevin reached out to Gottheimer’s office. His team contacted TAS and followed up to explain Kevin’s situation, including that his wife, Maryellen, had stopped working in January and that he had become her primary caregiver after she was hospitalized. In less than a month, Kevin’s refund of more than $7,000 was released. From his first call to a refund in hand, it took about a month. Kevin put it best: “This is how the government is supposed to work.”

David Mitnick of Glen Rock: David and his wife, Shelly Berger-Mitnick, reached out to Gottheimer’s office for help with their federal tax refund and a penalty abatement request. After the IRS audited them and found them ineligible for the energy tax credit they listed, they learned they were actually eligible for the credit in the following year. David repaid the previous year’s federal income tax amount in full, requested a penalty abatement, and filed an amended return, but after more than eight months, no refund or decision came. Gottheimer’s office contacted TAS right away and worked with David and their CPA to get TAS the forms and documents it asked for. Two months after they first called, the IRS confirmed $4,427.59 for their penalty abatement and $20,413.78 for their federal tax refund, more than $24,800 in total was sent to them.

If you are experiencing an issue with a federal agency, Gottheimer and his Constituent Services Team are here to listen and help with VA benefits, Social Security, Medicare, passports, delayed IRS refunds, and more. Reach out to Gottheimer in Fair Lawn at 201-389-1100, by email at HelpNJ5@mail.house.gov, or visitGottheimer.House.Gov for more information and resources.

title: Congressman Carter Condemns Haley Stevens’ Break with Democrats and Endorsement of GOP Candidate Mike Rogers
text:
Today, Congressman Carter released a statement following Haley Stevens’ endorsement of GOP Candidate Mike Rogers in the Michigan Senate race:

“In my opinion, Haley Stevens’s decision has more to do with a bruised ego than a commitment to the people she was elected to serve. I could not be more disappointed.

“I understand that losing a primary hurts. I also understand that policy disagreements can be deeply held. But when we seek public office, we accept a responsibility to put the people ahead of our own disappointment. That responsibility does not end when we lose an election or feel slighted by another candidate.

“Haley has chosen to endorse Republican Mike Rogers, whose Trump-style policies she once vehemently opposed. What changed for the families of Michigan? What changed about their need for affordable health care, good jobs, lower costs, and protection of their rights? Those needs remain, regardless of how she feels about the Democratic nominee.

“Antisemitism is serious, and we have an obligation to confront it. Dr. Abdul El-Sayed has said clearly that he disagrees with the contents of the outside group’s advertisement.

“Michigan Democrats chose their nominee. Haley had every right to challenge him in the primary and to continue pressing him on policy. But endorsing his Republican opponent days before the election calls into question the convictions she asked voters to believe in throughout her campaign.

“I have worked with colleagues with whom I strongly disagree. Public service requires that. We cannot allow a personal grievance to outweigh the consequences of our decisions for millions of people.

I expected better from my colleague. The people who supported her, volunteered for her, and trusted her word deserved better, too.”

title: Rep. Gabe Vasquez Announces the Birth of His Son
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – On November 1, 2026, U.S. Representative Gabe Vasquez (NM-02) and his fiancée, Nikki, announced they welcomed their first son to the world.

“Nikki and I are overjoyed to share that our son has arrived, and both Nikki and the baby are happy and healthy,” said Vasquez. “In these precious first few weeks, I will be supporting my family as we begin this new chapter together, and I look forward to bringing my perspective as a new dad to my work on behalf of all New Mexico families.”

As Vasquez spends time supporting his family and fulfilling his duties as a new dad, in the coming weeks, he will dedicate the majority of his time to his newborn. Vasquez will return to vote on the House floor as soon as possible, and his offices in Washington, Las Cruces, and Albuquerque will remain open and fully staffed to serve constituents across the district.

“Thank you to all of the New Mexicans and my colleagues in Congress who have shared their well wishes and kind words with Nikki and me. It means the world to our family and brings a renewed sense of public service to create a better future for all of our kids,” Vasquez added.

Vasquez supports policies to guarantee paid parental leave to all Americans and has introduced the Careworker Visa Act, a bill to bring down the cost of childcare for hardworking American families by creating commonsense legal pathways for immigrant careworkers.

title: Ansari Leads Bipartisan Effort in Demanding Answers on Care and Resettlement of Afghan Women and Children in Qatar
text:
WASHINGTON – Representatives Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03) and Don Bacon (NE-02) recently led a bipartisan effort calling on the Department of State and the Department of Homeland Security to provide urgent answers regarding the conditions and future resettlement plans for Afghan allies and their families currently housed at Camp As Sayliyah (CAS) in Doha, Qatar.

“Our Afghan allies stood alongside us, and we have the responsibility to ensure they and their families are treated with dignity and compassion,” said Rep. Ansari. “These women and children deserve access to medical care, education, and safe living conditions. We must uphold our country’s commitments and ensure these families have a clear path permanent resettlement and asylum. I’m glad to lead this bipartisan effort with my colleague, Congressman Don Bacon, to deliver the answers and accountability our Afghan allies deserve.”

“We made a commitment to the Afghan allies who stood alongside our servicemembers, and we have an obligation to honor it,” said Rep. Bacon. “We need clear answers about the care these families are receiving, particularly women and children, and the steps being taken to ensure their safe and orderly resettlement.”

With Afghan families enduring prolonged stays at CAS, the lawmakers are demanding accountability for the conditions they face and the services available to them. The letter calls for answers on access to essential maternal and OB-GYN care for pregnant women, routine pediatric services for young children, and safe, adequate living conditions. It also urges the provision of structured educational programming, English-language instruction, and recreational activities to support children’s development and well-being. Additionally, the lawmakers demand transparency around proposed third-country transfers, including clear assurances that any agreements uphold U.S. humanitarian standards, protect Afghan families’ well-being, and provide concrete pathways to safe, supported resettlement.

“More than 1,000 Afghan allies are waiting at Camp As Sayliyah, and most of them are women and children. They include family members of U.S. service members, and every one of them was brought there on an American promise. Representatives Ansari and Bacon are asking the right questions: Are pregnant women getting care? Are children learning? Is there a real path to resettlement? These families have kept their word to us, and they deserve clear answers and a way forward. AfghanEvac is grateful to every member who signed on,” said Shawn VanDiver, President and Founder of AfghanEvac.

“Last year, my team and I were at Camp As Sayliyah (CAS) helping secure flights and resettlement for hundreds of our wartime allies. Many of our allies, including the family members of U.S. veterans and service members, are still waiting for a safe path forward and still depend on health care and education at the camp,” said Andrew Sullivan, Executive Director of No One Left Behind. “We applaud this bipartisan recognition that a safe resolution for these allies, reached by Congress and the executive branch working in partnership, is in America’s best interest,” said Andrew Sullivan, Executive Director of No One Left Behind.

Ansari’s letter was cosigned by Representatives Don Bacon (NE-02), Jason Crow (CO-06), María Elvira Salazar (FL-27), Stephen F. Lynch (MA-08), Jasmine Crockett (TX-30), Diana DeGette (CO-01), Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-AL), Seth Moulton (MA-06), George Latimer (NY-16), James R. Walkinshaw (VA-11), Mike Quigley (IL-05), Adelita S. Grijalva (AZ-07), Ami Bera (CA-06), Deborah K. Ross (NC-02), Julia Brownley (CA-26), Veronica Escobar (TX-16), Emily Randall (WA-06), Jennifer L. McClellan (VA-04), William R. Keating (MA-09), Dina Titus (NV-01), and Sara Jacobs (CA-51).

The letter is also endorsed by One Left Behind, AfghanEvac, Afghans For A Better Tomorrow, Association of Wartime Allies (AWA), FAER, With Honor, USAHello, Center for Gender & Refugee Studies, Borderlands Resource Initiative, Human Rights First, Humanitarian Legal Assistance Project, Special Operations Association of America (SOAA), Refugee Council USA (RCUSA), Lawyers for Good Government, Feminist Majority, Frontera Federation, Keeping Our Promise Inc., Instant Aid, Cross Cultural Communications, LLC, Iraq and Afghanistan Veterans of America, Hearts & Homes for Refugees, Unitarian Universalists for Social Justice, The 5ive Pillars Organization, Allied Shepherd, International Institute of New England, Dialogue Center for Resilience and Empowerment (DCRE), Paws Unite People Inc, SunEx Aviation, Our Culture is Giving, U.S. Committee for Refugees and Immigrants, Asian Americans Advancing Justice Southern California, Afghan Scout Relief Fund, Afghan Advantage, Global Refuge, Union for Reform Judaism, and Immigrant Defenders Law Center.

Read the letter HERE and below.

Dear Secretary Rubio and Secretary Mullin,

We write to follow up on the ongoing transit operations at Camp As Sayliyah (CAS) in Doha, Qatar, where Afghan allies and their families remain in temporary housing awaiting final resettlement processing. In particular, we wish to learn more about the conditions faced by the hundreds of women and the young children currently in processing at the facility, and to request an update on plans for their safe resettlement.

These individuals were brought out of Afghanistan on U.S.-provided flights with the promise and understanding that CAS would serve as a short-term transit hub for temporary stay in the final stages of their processing for secure resettlement to the United States. With this sacred promise to the heroes who supported our forces in Afghanistan at the heart of our inquiry, we want to ensure that the most vulnerable among those at CAS receive the necessary processing support, health care, and clear communications on their next steps.

Health and Support Services for Women and Children

Given the extended stays for many families, maintaining adequate specialized care remains a priority. We request an assessment of the medical services available at CAS, particularly maternal and OBGYN health resources for pregnant women and routine pediatric care for young children. Ensuring appropriate living conditions and consistent medical oversight for these families is essential as their immigration processing moves forward.

Educational Opportunities and Developmental Support for Children

Beyond immediate health and security considerations, we also ask for an evaluation of the educational and developmental resources available to the school-aged children residing at CAS. Given the extended length of stay for many families, access to structured educational programming, English language learning, and recreational activities is essential to minimize learning disruptions and support childhood development. Ensuring there are routine learning environments at the facility not only helps prepare these children for integration into American schools and communities, but also provides critical stability and psychological support during a period of prolonged transition.

Pathways to Final Resettlement

Clear and transparent communication regarding resettlement pathways is vital for maintaining the trust of our allies now and in future engagements. We ask for clarification on the open U.S. Refugee Admissions Program (USRAP) P-1/P-2 applications and family reunification cases at CAS. Additionally, we request information on how the Department of State and the Department of Homeland Security are handling any proposed third-country transfers to ensure the underlying bilateral agreements align with U.S. humanitarian standards and provide established resettlement support in the receiving country.

To inform Congress’ collaboration with your departments to shape an effective path forward, we

request your response addressing the following questions by November 27, 2026:

What medical care is available for the Afghan evacuees at CAS, particularly maternal and OBGYN health resources for pregnant women and routine pediatric care for young children?

What learning support is available to school aged children? What cultural and educational resources are available to prepare adults for employment and resettlement in the United States?

How many individuals have ongoing USRAP referrals? What resources do your departments need to ensure all these individuals can renew their requisite documents and medical panels?

What specific steps are your departments taking to communicate the status of resettlement options (including USRAP and third country agreements) to the individuals at CAS?

Thank you for your continued work to uphold U.S. national security by fulfilling our commitments to Afghan allies and their families. We look forward to working with your departments to ensure a swift, safe, and organized resolution for those at CAS.

Sincerely,

Yassamin Ansari

Member of Congress

Follow @RepYassAnsari on all social media platforms and visit Ansari.House.gov to learn more.

title: Baumgartner Releases Healthy Forests Incentives Act to Reduce Wildfire Risk
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congressman Michael Baumgartner (WA-05) released the text of his Healthy Forests Incentives Act of 2026, legislation to reduce wildfire risk by connecting long-term forest stewardship with targeted incentives for businesses that put removed wood to productive use.

“Today, many of our Western forests have up to 7 times thicker tree density than they did 100 years ago,” said Congressman Baumgartner. “These levels of unhealthy fuel loads contribute to extreme fire risk, particularly in forested areas near residential areas. My legislation creates incentives and a pathway to clear out these dangerous forests by harvesting timber in targeted areas. We must take action now to reduce risks for the next, possible catastrophic forest fire. We lost more than 700 homes this summer, I don’t want us losing another 700 next year,” he said.

“By connecting long-term stewardship in high-risk areas with incentives for businesses that use the wood we remove, this bill makes prevention a sustained economic activity—not just a series of isolated federal projects,” Baumgartner continued.

Over the past 10 years, Congress appropriated $64.7 billion in wildfire-specific funds, with more than half directed toward response and only 17 percent toward mitigation. “My bill seeks to better target federal resources toward preventive restoration in high-risk landscapes, while reviving forest economies across the west with more energy, jobs and cutting-edge building materials,” Baumgartner concluded.

title: Bonamici, Wyden, Merkley Demand Investigation into ICE Tire Slashing Incident
text:
WASHINGTON, DC [11/2/26] – Today Congresswoman Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01) and Senators Ron Wyden and Jeff Merkley demanded an investigation into Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents for slashing a couple’s tires in Hillsboro.

The couple was observing and recording ICE agents in a supermarket parking lot on October 7, 2026, before multiple masked ICE agents in three vehicles tailed the couple, boxed them in, and repeatedly stabbed and slashed their tires before driving away. A video of the incident can be viewed here.

“ICE agents cannot act with impunity,” the lawmakers wrote. “The First Amendment protects the right to observe, gather information, and record law enforcement officers performing their duties in public. These constitutional protections are necessary for the public to learn about and freely debate the government’s actions, including potential misconduct, and demand accountability when necessary.”

The lawmakers noted that there have been many documented cases of excessive use of force and intimidation tactics against peaceful community members and legal observers by ICE in Oregon and across the country. They called for the Inspector General for the Department of Homeland Security to immediately investigate the Oct. 7 incident in Hillsboro, identify the agents involved, and preserve all evidence, so that those responsible may be disciplined.

“Without videos from bystanders, observers, journalists, and protestors, the public would never know the full scale of federal retaliation against those who seek to document ICE activity,” the lawmakers wrote.

Bonamici, Wyden, Merkley, and Dexter also recently raised concerns about the lack of access to counsel for individuals detained by ICE and what appear to be new protocols for bypassing the Portland ICE facility entirely. That letter can be found here.

The full letter about the Oct. 7 incident can be read here and below:

Dear Inspector General Cuffari:

We write to request an investigation into an alarming incident that occurred on October 7, 2026, in which U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents harassed, intimidated, and retaliated against a couple in Hillsboro, Oregon for engaging in First Amendment activities. The incident occurred when our constituents observed and recorded ICE agents in a supermarket parking lot. Soon thereafter, multiple masked ICE agents in three vehicles recklessly tailed the couple, boxed them in, and dangerously vandalized their vehicle by repeatedly stabbing and puncturing one of their tires before driving away.1

ICE agents cannot act with impunity. The First Amendment protects the right to observe, gather information about, and record law enforcement officers performing their duties in public.2 These constitutional protections are necessary for the public to learn about and freely debate the government’s actions, including potential misconduct, and demand accountability when necessary.

Since President Trump returned to office in January 2025, federal ICE agents across the country have repeatedly failed to respect rights afforded under the Constitution, especially the First Amendment. We have seen many documented cases of excessive use of force and intimidation tactics by ICE in Oregon, including federal agents needlessly deploying tear-gas and other projectiles against peaceful community members as well as driving erratically and verbally threatening legal observers. This pattern of irresponsible and illegal behavior from federal agents is also evident across the country. For example, federal agents in Memphis, Tennessee harassed observers by swerving at them, tailing them, boxing them in, and pulling them over without reasonable suspicion; sitting outside of their homes; and assaulting and arresting them.3 In Los Angeles, federal agents fired crowd control weapons into the heads and other sensitive areas of observers, journalists, and protestors. A judge later granted an injunction against this behavior4 and found that the plaintiffs have plausibly alleged that DHS had a policy of retaliating against people who record the activities of agents.5

Most troubling, federal immigration agents killed Alex Pretti while he was peacefully recording and protesting ICE’s actions.6 Through all of this, the Trump administration has repeatedly covered up officer misconduct and obstructed investigations.7 To this day, there is no evidence that the federal government has meaningfully investigated Mr. Pretti’s killing, with his parents noting that “at every turn, they have ignored us, misled us and shielded Alex’s killers.”8 This reckless behavior and senseless violence endangers everyone across the country and does not advance ICE’s mission of enforcing immigration laws to preserve national security and public safety.

Without videos from bystanders, observers, journalists, and protestors, the public would never know the full scale of federal retaliation against those who seek to document ICE activity.

We hereby demand that your offices immediately undertake an investigation of the October 7, 2026, incident in Hillsboro, Oregon outlined above. Please identify the ICE agents involved and preserve all relevant evidence so the officers can be disciplined and prosecuted as appropriate.

Further, we request that you undertake a comprehensive investigation of the pervasive pattern of ICE agents acting unlawfully and retaliating against individuals exercising their First Amendment rights. We ask that you work with Congress to make lasting changes to ICE training, oversight, and accountability. The rights of our constituents must not be jeopardized any longer.

Sincerely,

title: Oregon Delegation Celebrates Federal Support for Oregon’s Hazelnut, Seafood Industries
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, Oregon’s U.S. Senator Jeff Merkley led Oregon Congressional Delegation members—including Senator Ron Wyden and U.S. Representatives Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), Val Hoyle (OR-04), Andrea Salinas (OR-06), Maxine Dexter (OR-03), and Janelle Bynum (OR-05)—to announce that after pressure from the delegation, the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) will purchase hazelnuts and Pacific Whiting fillets under the agency’s Section 32 purchase program. These purchases will benefit communities and rural economies across Oregon by supporting domestic production and distribution of these agricultural goods during periods of significant market disruption and economic uncertainty.

“Our fisheries and farms deliver incredible products all around the world and are the lifeblood of our communities,” said Merkley, who led the Oregon delegation in pressing USDA to include hazelnuts and whiting in its latest food purchase. “This announcement ensures Oregon’s harvesters, processors, and producers will receive critical financial assistance needed to continue operating and providing services here in Oregon and beyond. I am elated the USDA has decided to make these purchases—this is a win for communities across our state.”

“Iconic state industries like agriculture and fishing count on the U.S. Department of Agriculture to do its job and support Oregonians working hard to keep producing their world-class goods,” said Wyden. “I’m glad the full-court press from the delegation has unlocked this win for Oregonians fishing Pacific whiting and growing hazelnuts.”

“Oregonians know that hazelnuts and seafood are some of the state’s most popular and delicious products,” said Bonamici. “Our growers and producers work tirelessly and bolster the local economy. I’m glad the USDA is making this investment.”

“These investments from the USDA will support the people who harvest, process and bring Pacific Whiting fish and hazelnuts to market,” said Hoyle. “By putting Oregon fishermen and farmers first, we’re boosting our coastal and rural economies."

“Oregon’s specialty crop growers are the backbone of our economy, but too many are struggling with rising costs and uncertain markets,” said Salinas. “In the Willamette Valley, generations of farmers have depended on the hazelnut industry for their livelihoods. That’s why I joined my colleagues in pushing USDA to purchase Oregon hazelnuts and Pacific whiting. These purchases will provide much-needed support for our growers and fishing communities while putting more Oregon-grown and Oregon-caught food onto kitchen tables. I’m proud we secured this win for Oregon producers, and I’ll keep fighting to make sure our specialty crop farmers have the markets and resources they need to succeed.”

"Oregon’s farmers and fishermen work hard to feed our communities, and they deserve a federal government that stands behind them,” said Dexter. “Our delegation pushed USDA to act, and these $34 million in purchases will support Oregon’s hazelnut growers and fishermen during a difficult economic stretch. This investment will help sustain local jobs, strengthen rural and coastal economies, and get nutritious food to families who need it.”

“Our farmers are putting in the work every day to keep Oregon families fed,” said Bynum. “And they’re not just helping put food on the table, they’re keeping money with our families, creating good jobs close to home, and giving people what they need to put down roots here in Oregon. Money back in our state and with our farmers is a win-win.”

title: Salinas, Bonamici, Merkley, Wyden Secure over $500,000 for Tualatin Soil and Water Conservation District
text:
Tualatin, OR — Today, Congresswomen Andrea Salinas (OR-06) and Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), alongside Oregon Senators Ron Wyden and Jeff Merkley, announced they secured the release of over $530,000 in federal funding from the Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS) to support Tualatin Soil and Water Conservation District (TSWCD).

In 2022, TSWCD applied to the NRCS for funding to improve fish habitat in Washington County. This work included replacing deteriorated culverts with bridges and modern culverts that help threatened species like steelhead trout move through local waterways. In February 2024, NRCS approved and obligated $1,074,887 to reimburse TSWCD for their work.

As of early September 2026, NRCS had only paid $543,837 of the over $1.07 million they had promised to TSWCD. This $531,000 shortfall has severely challenged TSWCD’s budget and would have stuck the taxpayers of Washington County with the bill. Following outreach from the Oregon delegation, NRSC honored its commitment and released the final sum to TSWCD.

“When Oregonians make a promise, we keep it. The federal government should be held to the same standard,” said Rep. Salinas. “Tualatin Soil and Water did the work to improve our waterways, and Washington County taxpayers should never have been left holding the bag. I’m glad we got this money out the door and where it belongs.”

“Supporting threatened species and their habitats reflects Oregon values and our commitment to environmental protection, and I was grateful when the Tualatin Soil and Water Conservation District secured federal funds to improve fish habitat in Washington County,” said Rep. Bonamici. “Unfortunately, the Trump administration paid only about half of the promised funding, leaving Washington County taxpayers to pick up the balance. I’m glad that my colleagues and I were able to help resolve this issue and secure all the funds the water conservation district needed for the project."

“Thanks to our efforts, this funding is finally moving forward and will help ensure the Tualatin Soil and Water Conservation District can continue its work to improve waterways in Washington County,” said Sen. Merkley. “Oregon’s native fish are the lifeblood of our state, supporting the health and vitality of our communities, local economies, and Tribes who have been here since time immemorial. I’ll keep pushing to secure the necessary federal funds to protect our state’s ecosystems for generations to come.”

“I’m glad the full-court press by the delegation unlocked these resources promised by the federal government to the Tualatin Soil and Water Conservation District,” Wyden said. “These funds will keep waterways improvements on track, helping with water quality and fish habitat alike in Washington County.”

title: Reps. Castro, Vasquez, Cisneros Introduce Resolution Recognizing Hispanic and Latino Servicemembers
text:

While Hispanic and Latino servicemembers account for the largest growing population across the military, they are too often overlooked for leadership roles, and that needs to improve. Our forces are at their best when they reflect our nation’s diversity.”

“The Hispanic community has proudly demonstrated its pride and willingness to serve our nation for decades, diversifying our ranks and strengthening our national defense,” said Congressman Vasquez. “In New Mexico, that tradition runs deep — we are a state of proud Americans who answer the call. title: “A key source of innovation in our fight against Lyme disease”Smith congratulates Lakewood constituent and winner of LymeX Visible Voices Prize
text:
Rep. Chris Smith (R-NJ), the founder and Co-Chair of the Congressional Lyme and Tick-Borne Disease Caucus, welcomed U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s announcement of the 16 winners of the LymeX Visible Voices Prize, including YMD from Lakewood Township.

Smith noted that one of the winners, YMD—based in his congressional district in Lakewood, NJ—created a card that allows patients to organize their symptom histories, enabling them to better communicate their experiences to their clinicians.

“I want to extend my congratulations and thanks to all the winners of the LymeX Visible Voices Prize for their outstanding submissions—including and especially NJ-04’s very own, YMD,” said Smith. “The initiatives launched by this effort will help public to identify and prevent tick bites, as well as empower physicians to better treat patients with Lyme and other tick-borne diseases.”

The Lyme X Visible Voices Prize—a competition sponsored by the LymeX Innovation Accelerator, a public private partnership between HHS and the Steven & Alexandra Cohen Foundation—challenged participants to develop creative ways to improve understanding and visibility of Lyme disease and other tick-borne diseases.

The winning submissions—which include educational resources for care providers, as well as interactive educational platforms for the general public—will each receive a share of the $250,000 total prize amount. For their impressive invention, YMD received an “Impact Award,” valued at $10,000.

“The LymeX Innovation Accelerator has been a key source of innovation in our fight against Lyme disease. By engaging a variety of private and public sector stakeholders to advance diagnostics and treatments, we get closer to our ultimate goal of finding a lasting cure for Lyme disease,” noted Smith, who has previously secured millions of dollars in federal funding for the continuation of the program.

“It is time for Congress to follow Secretary Kennedy’s example and codify the LymeX program, ensuring sustained funding for future breakthroughs,” he continued.

Smith is the author of the LymeX Authorization Act (HR 7482), which would codify and authorize $5 million towards the LymeX Innovation Accelerator. Since its establishment in 2018, LymeX has played a critical role in advancing federal research for patient-centered Lyme treatments and diagnostics.

In January of last year, LymeX completed its third phase, which saw six teams plan and present their clinical performance studies and publicize their diagnostic tests. A total of five winning teams received a share of the total Phase 3 award of $2.1 million.

In March, LymeX commenced its fourth phase, wherein teams will submit summary papers on their study results and commercialization plans. Phase 4 winners can expect to receive a share of the corresponding $3 million dedicated to this stage.

In December of 2025, Smith attended and served as a key panelist at the HHS’ Lyme Disease Roundtable, where Secretary Kennedy announced the $10 million renewal of the LymeX Innovation Accelerator.

title: Thirty Armed Services Democrats, Veterans, Raise Alarm Over March Attack on NSA Bahrain, Pentagon’s Poor Treatment of Evacuated Military Families
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, 30 members of Congress signed on to a letter demanding action and answers from the Pentagon about the poor treatment of military servicemembers and their families who were evacuated from Naval Support Activity Bahrain (NSA Bahrain) in March 2026.

This letter comes after MS NOW reported on the details of a hasty and traumatic evacuation from NSA Bahrain in March, noting that many military family members have been living out of hotels and short-term rentals and are being required to pay out of pocket to cover these expenses. The letter demands that the Department of Defense right this wrong and support these evacuated military families.

The members of Congress also asked the Secretary how much it would cost to repair the severe damage to NSA Bahrain and how the incapacitation of the base has impacted U.S. operations in the Iran War and the wider Middle East.

The letter is co-led by Congressman Chris Deluzio (PA-17), Congressman Pat Ryan (NY-18), and Senator Richard Blumenthal (CT). The letter signatories are members of the House Armed Services Committee, the Senate Armed Services Committee, or are members of the Democratic Veterans Caucus.

The letter reads, “President Trump launched the Iran War on February 28th before evacuating the roughly 8,300 military personnel, DoD civilians, and their families stationed at NSA Bahrain. Families were authorized to evacuate only after the war started, subjecting them to the Iranian retaliatory strikes that heavily damaged the base. Since March, these evacuees have been under constant emotional, financial, and psychological stress... While the Department of Defense has provided safe haven entitlements to offset the cost of living for evacuees, this funding is scheduled to be terminated in November or after the 180th day of receiving the entitlement, before many have found permanent housing and transportation.”

The members continue, “Because NSA Bahrain was a critical logistics hub for U.S. Central Command, we require a better understanding of how the severe damage to the base has impacted U.S. operations… We have significant concerns about the morale and welfare of the troops deployed to the region, especially in light of the reporting on the conditions onboard the USS Gerald R. Ford and USS Abraham Lincoln, which both served record breaking deployments.”

Specifically, the members requested answers by November 13, 2026 to the following questions:

Why was the Navy’s request to extend the safe haven entitlements for evacuees denied?

Who made this decision?

Why are safe haven entitlements for evacuees being terminated before the arrival of household goods?

What will the Department of Defense do to ensure that evacuees from NSA Bahrain are not paying out of pocket for living expenses incurred by the evacuation?

What processes, if any, are in place for evacuees to receive reimbursement for expenses incurred, and how many reimbursement cases are pending?

Given the damage to NSA Bahrain, which logistic hub (or hubs) has the Department of Defense been using amidst the Iran War?

What has been the operational impact of the loss of NSA Bahrain?

Does the Department of Defense intend to repair and rebuild NSA Bahrain?

If so, how much is the expected cost for such work?

What is the financial cost of the damage to NSA Bahrain?

The House signatories of the letter are: Reps. Chris Deluzio (PA-17, co-lead), Pat Ryan (NY-18, co-lead), Wesley Bell (MO-01), Salud Carbajal (CA-24), Gil Cisneros (CA-31), Herb Conaway (NJ-03), Joe Courtney (CT-02), Jason Crow (CO-06), Sarah Elfreth (MD-03), John Garamendi (CA-08), Maggie Goodlander (NH-02), Chrissy Houlahan (PA-06), Sara Jacobs (CA-51), Bill Keating (MA-09), Ro Khanna (CA-17), Ted Lieu (CA-36), Jimmy Panetta (CA-19), Adam Smith (WA-09), Eric Sorensen (IL-17), Marilyn Strickland (WA-10), Mike Thompson (CA-04), Derek Tran (CA-45), Eugene Vindman (VA-07), and George Whitesides (CA-27).

The Senate signatories of the letter are: Sens. Richard Blumenthal (CT, co-lead), Tammy Duckworth (IL), Kirstin Gillibrand (NY), Mazie Hirono (HI), Jacky Rosen (NV), Elizabeth Warren (MA).

The full text of the letter is below and is linked here.

Dear Secretary Hegseth:

We write to raise concern over reporting that servicemembers and their families are continuing to face significant hardship following their evacuation from Naval Support Activity Bahrain (NSA Bahrain) in March this year. Additionally, we seek to better understand how the incapacitation of NSA Bahrain has impacted U.S. operations in the Iran War and the broader Middle East. In an August town hall, Chief of Naval Operations, Adm. Daryl Caudle, said that the Navy would not be using NSA Bahrain for the foreseeable future. This is significant not only for the thousands of servicemembers and their families personally involved, but also because NSA Bahrain is a critical logistics hub that has served as the headquarters for U.S. Naval Forces Central Command and U.S. Navy Fifth Fleet since 1995.

Servicemembers and Their Families are Not Receiving Adequate Support

As you know, President Trump launched the Iran War on February 28th before evacuating the roughly 8,300 military personnel, DoD civilians, and their families stationed at NSA Bahrain. Families were authorized to evacuate only after the war started, subjecting them to the Iranian retaliatory strikes that heavily damaged the base. Since March, these evacuees have been under constant emotional, financial, and psychological stress. Some have had to move across continents, stay in temporary lodging for months, enroll their children in a new school mid-year, pay out of pocket for significant costs associated with a move and more, all often without access to belongings they were forced to leave behind. While the Department of Defense has provided safe haven entitlements to offset the cost of living for evacuees, this funding is scheduled to be terminated in November or after the 180th day of receiving the entitlement, before many have found permanent housing and transportation.

In a recent town hall, Navy officials relayed that your Department of Defense leadership had denied a request to extend the safe haven entitlements, and that each evacuee had to seek individual approval from the Acting Secretary of the Navy. This is unacceptable. To make matters worse, the signing of a lease is being used as a triggering event for termination of the safe haven entitlement. This is bad policy. Although a family may have signed a lease for a permanent residence, they may still have to use a rental vehicle or stay in temporary lodging while they wait for their household goods to arrive from overseas. Requiring servicemembers to pay out of pocket for expenses that were forced upon them by your mismanagement of the Iran War is wrong. You must fix this.

Loss of NSA Bahrain and U.S. Presence in the Middle East

As the Iran War reaches the ninth month, our constituents have expressed increasing concern about the cost of the conflict and the lack of transparency surrounding U.S. operations and strategic goals in the region. Because NSA Bahrain was a critical logistics hub for U.S. Central Command, we require a better understanding of how the severe damage to the base has impacted U.S. operations. In August, the New York Times reported that the U.S Navy is now resupplying from Diego Garcia, an island in the Indian Ocean 2,200 miles away from the Persian Gulf. We have significant concerns about the morale and welfare of the troops deployed to the region, especially in light of the reporting on the conditions onboard the USS Gerald R. Ford and USS Abraham Lincoln, which both served record breaking deployments.

In executing the Congress’s oversight authority under Article I of the Constitution, we request answers to the following questions by November 13, 2026.

Why was the Navy’s request to extend the safe haven entitlements for evacuees denied?

Who made this decision?

Why are safe haven entitlements for evacuees being terminated before the arrival of household goods?

What will the Department of Defense do to ensure that evacuees from NSA Bahrain are not paying out of pocket for living expenses incurred by the evacuation?

What processes, if any, are in place for evacuees to receive reimbursement for expenses incurred, and how many reimbursement cases are pending?

Given the damage to NSA Bahrain, which logistic hub (or hubs) has the Department of Defense been using amidst the Iran War?

What has been the operational impact of the loss of NSA Bahrain?

Does the Department of Defense intend to repair and rebuild NSA Bahrain?

If so, how much is the expected cost for such work?

What is the financial cost of the damage to NSA Bahrain?

title: Gallagher Demands Accountability Following Audit Exposing Billions in Questionable Medi-Cal Billing
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman James Gallagher (CA-01) joined Congressman Jay Obernolte (CA-23) and fellow members of California's congressional delegation in demanding answers from the California Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) following a troubling state audit that revealed significant failures in oversight of the state's Medi-Cal program.

In a letter to DHCS Director Michelle Baass, the lawmakers raised serious concerns about California's failure to investigate thousands of providers flagged for potentially improper billing and recover hundreds of millions of dollars in overpayments. The findings raise questions about the state's management of taxpayer funds intended to provide health care to millions of vulnerable Californians.

According to an October 15 report from the California State Auditor, DHCS identified approximately 28,000 Medi-Cal providers as high risk for potentially improper billing during fiscal year 2024–2025. Despite these warning signs, the department had not initiated referrals or investigations for more than 26,000 of those providers, which collectively accounted for at least $12 billion in Medi-Cal services.

The audit also found that DHCS identified more than $2 billion in provider overpayments between fiscal years 2020 and 2025, approximately $300 million of which remain unrecovered.

“California taxpayers are pouring billions of dollars into Medi-Cal, and they deserve to know that money is being spent responsibly, not lost to fraud, waste, and bad oversight,” said Congressman Gallagher. “The State Auditor’s findings raise serious questions about why thousands of high-risk providers went without further investigation and why hundreds of millions of dollars in overpayments remain unrecovered. We cannot afford to ignore these warning signs. Period. Medi-Cal must protect the vulnerable Californians who depend on it, and that starts with holding the system accountable, rooting out fraud, and ensuring taxpayer dollars go toward legitimate patient care.”

The audit's findings come as California faces additional federal scrutiny over its management of Medi-Cal. On October 20, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) announced it would defer an additional $1.2 billion in federal Medicaid payments to California over concerns about documentation supporting certain program expenditures.

The lawmakers are requesting information about DHCS's efforts to strengthen oversight of Medi-Cal, investigate potentially fraudulent billing practices, and recover improper payments.

“Medi-Cal provides critical care to millions of Californians, and every dollar lost to fraud is a dollar that is not available to help our most vulnerable citizens access the care they need,” said Congressman Obernolte. “California taxpayers deserve to know that their money is being used wisely and appropriately. Stronger oversight is necessary to prevent fraud, waste, and abuse while protecting the patients who depend on this critical program.”

Gallagher joined Representatives Ken Calvert (CA-41), Tom McClintock (CA-05), David Valadao (CA-22), Young Kim (CA-40), and Vince Fong (CA-20) in signing the letter led by Obernolte.

The lawmakers are calling for greater transparency and stronger accountability to protect taxpayer dollars while preserving access to care for Californians who rely on Medi-Cal.

title: Comisionado Residente presenta comentarios sobre las reglas propuestas para el Censo 2030 y su impacto en Puerto Rico
text:
Caguas, Puerto Rico — El Comisionado Residente Pablo José Hernández presentó comentarios ante el Negociado del Censo de Estados Unidos para advertir sobre los posibles efectos de las reglas propuestas para el Censo 2030 en la contabilización de la población de Puerto Rico y de las comunidades puertorriqueñas en Estados Unidos.

El 30 de octubre, Hernández firmó junto a otros miembros del Congreso una carta dirigida al Negociado del Censo en la que expresaron su oposición a la propuesta y solicitaron su retiro. La comunicación planteó preocupaciones sobre los nuevos criterios de residencia, el uso de récords administrativos y las restricciones a la recopilación de información sobre raza, origen étnico y orientación sexual. En sus comentarios específicos sobre Puerto Rico, el Comisionado Residente detalla cómo estos cambios podrían afectar el conteo de nuestra población.

“Nos preocupa que esta propuesta limite la información demográfica esencial que se recopila sobre nuestra población. Sin datos precisos, se hace más difícil identificar las necesidades de nuestras comunidades y priorizar lo básico: los servicios, los recursos y la atención que nuestra gente necesita. Por eso, me opuse a esta regla y solicité su retiro”, expresó el Comisionado Residente.

Entre sus señalamientos, Hernández advierte que utilizar únicamente récords contributivos federales podría excluir a residentes bona fide de Puerto Rico que no tienen obligación de radicar una planilla federal. Por ello, plantea considerar también información del Departamento de Hacienda, incluidos los formularios W-2PR. Asimismo, señala que los sistemas automatizados podrían dejar fuera hogares en comunidades rurales cuyas direcciones no siguen los formatos convencionales.

Los comentarios también cuestionan las posibles restricciones a las preguntas sobre raza y origen hispano, cuya información permite identificar a las comunidades puertorriqueñas dentro y fuera de la Isla. Además, señalan la importancia de considerar los movimientos de personas entre Puerto Rico y los estados para evitar que sean omitidas o contadas incorrectamente.

La importancia de un conteo preciso queda reflejada en los resultados de 2020. Según el propio Negociado del Censo, en el Censo de 2020 se estima que aproximadamente 217,000 residentes de Puerto Rico, equivalentes al 7.1% de la población estimada en hogares, fueron omitidos del conteo.

Los datos del Censo ayudan al Gobierno de Puerto Rico a planificar los servicios que necesitan los municipios y las comunidades, revisar los distritos legislativos y administrar programas federales. Por eso, Hernández plantea que las reglas del Censo 2030 deben evitar que Puerto Rico y su población queden insuficientemente representados en la información oficial.

title: Oregon Delegation Celebrates Federal Support for Oregon’s Hazelnut, Seafood Industries
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, Oregon’s U.S. Senator Jeff Merkley led Oregon Congressional Delegation members—including Senator Ron Wyden and U.S. Representatives Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), Val Hoyle (OR-04), Andrea Salinas (OR-06), Maxine Dexter (OR-03), and Janelle Bynum (OR-05)—to announce that after pressure from the delegation, the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) will purchase hazelnuts and Pacific Whiting fillets under the agency’s Section 32 purchase program. These purchases will benefit communities and rural economies across Oregon by supporting domestic production and distribution of these agricultural goods during periods of significant market disruption and economic uncertainty.

“Our fisheries and farms deliver incredible products all around the world and are the lifeblood of our communities,” said Merkley, who led the Oregon delegation in pressing USDA to include hazelnuts and whiting in its latest food purchase. “This announcement ensures Oregon’s harvesters, processors, and producers will receive critical financial assistance needed to continue operating and providing services here in Oregon and beyond. I am elated the USDA has decided to make these purchases—this is a win for communities across our state.”

“Iconic state industries like agriculture and fishing count on the U.S. Department of Agriculture to do its job and support Oregonians working hard to keep producing their world-class goods,” said Wyden. “I’m glad the full-court press from the delegation has unlocked this win for Oregonians fishing Pacific whiting and growing hazelnuts.”

“Oregonians know that hazelnuts and seafood are some of the state’s most popular and delicious products,” said Bonamici. “Our growers and producers work tirelessly and bolster the local economy. I’m glad the USDA is making this investment.”

“These investments from the USDA will support the people who harvest, process and bring Pacific Whiting fish and hazelnuts to market,” said Hoyle. “By putting Oregon fishermen and farmers first, we’re boosting our coastal and rural economies."

“Oregon’s specialty crop growers are the backbone of our economy, but too many are struggling with rising costs and uncertain markets,” said Salinas. “In the Willamette Valley, generations of farmers have depended on the hazelnut industry for their livelihoods. That’s why I joined my colleagues in pushing USDA to purchase Oregon hazelnuts and Pacific whiting. These purchases will provide much-needed support for our growers and fishing communities while putting more Oregon-grown and Oregon-caught food onto kitchen tables. I’m proud we secured this win for Oregon producers, and I’ll keep fighting to make sure our specialty crop farmers have the markets and resources they need to succeed.”

"Oregon’s farmers and fishermen work hard to feed our communities, and they deserve a federal government that stands behind them,” said Dexter. “Our delegation pushed USDA to act, and these $34 million in purchases will support Oregon’s hazelnut growers and fishermen during a difficult economic stretch. This investment will help sustain local jobs, strengthen rural and coastal economies, and get nutritious food to families who need it.”

“Our farmers are putting in the work every day to keep Oregon families fed,” said Bynum. “And they’re not just helping put food on the table, they’re keeping money with our families, creating good jobs close to home, and giving people what they need to put down roots here in Oregon. Money back in our state and with our farmers is a win-win.”

Previously, Merkley and the Oregon delegation pressed the USDA to include Pacific whiting and Oregon hazelnuts, which account for 99 percent of hazelnuts produced in the United States, in this year’s Section 32 purchases. Following their efforts, the USDA announced it was purchasing $22 million in hazelnuts and $12 million in Pacific whiting.

title: Smith Helps Secure More Than $12.5 Million to Modernize Rural Health Care in Missouri’s 8th District
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – The Trump Administration recently announced more than $12.5 million in federal investment to modernize rural health care services and expand access to care in Missouri’s 8th Congressional District. This funding is part of the Rural Health Transformation Program’s (RHTP) historic $50 billion investment in rural health care which Rep. Jason Smith (MO-08) authored as part of the Working Families Tax Cuts, also known as the One, Big, Beautiful Bill.

“I wrote the Rural Health Transformation Program to benefit Missouri communities. When a rural hospital shuts down back home, that often means losing half a day on the road for a basic scan, mental health appointment, or prenatal checkup,” said Rep. Jason Smith. “We’ve already seen a dozen rural hospitals close across Missouri in the last ten years alone, and I made it my mission to make sure that doesn’t continue. This investment is yet another sign that the program is doing exactly what I intended it to do when I included it in the One, Big, Beautiful Bill. I’m thrilled to see this much-needed funding go to several providers back home to improve and protect rural health care across southeast and south central Missouri, and I’ll keep fighting to ensure that our neighbors have access to the care they need and deserve.”

“President Trump understands that every American deserves high-quality healthcare, no matter where they live,” said Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. “We are putting resources directly into rural communities to strengthen the health workforce, modernize infrastructure, expand access, and bring care closer to home. We are giving states the flexibility to build solutions around the people they serve, while demanding accountability for results. That is how we strengthen rural health, improve the lives of patients and families, and Make America Healthy Again.”

“Instead of throwing money at a broken status quo, President Trump’s Rural Health Transformation Program is funding the structural improvements necessary to build stronger, more sustainable rural health systems,” said Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz. “These investments are already delivering better access to higher-quality care for rural Missourians, and we look forward to working with state leaders to build on that success over the remaining four years of the program.”

“Every Missourian deserves access to quality healthcare close to home,” said Gov. Mike Kehoe. “These investments will help rural health care providers modernize facilities, expand maternal and behavioral health services, and strengthen access to critical care across our state. By supporting locally driven solutions, we are helping rural communities build a stronger health care system that improves outcomes for Missouri families today and for generations to come.”

title: Kean Introduces Bill to Create New Grants for Emergency Medical Services
text:
(November 2, 2026) WASHINGTON, D.C. – Last week, Congressman Tom Kean, Jr. (NJ-07) introduced the EMS SUPPORT Act of 2026 to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services to make grants for facility upgrades, equipment, training, or services for EMS personnel.

“During a medical emergency, you deserve the highest level of care from the most qualified first responders with the best possible resources,” said Congressman Kean. “That is why I introduced the EMS SUPPORT Act to create a grant program and ensure that EMTs have the training and tools that they need to help individuals when they need it most.”

“As both a Town of Clinton Councilman and Trustee of South Branch Emergency Services, I have seen firsthand the growing challenges facing emergency medical services across New Jersey and throughout our country,” said Clinton Councilman Ross Traphagen. “Our EMS agencies are being asked to respond to more emergencies than ever before, while struggling with rising operational costs, staffing shortages, and the financial burden of maintaining lifesaving equipment and ambulances. I strongly support Congressman Tom Kean Jr.’s EMS SUPPORT Act because it recognizes that reliable emergency medical services are not a luxury - they are an essential public service. By creating new federal funding opportunities for staffing, training, equipment, and infrastructure, this legislation would provide meaningful support to the men and women who answer the call when our communities need them most, while helping ease the financial pressure on local taxpayers. Every resident deserves to know that when they dial 911, a trained EMS crew will be there. This legislation is an important step toward ensuring that our EMS organizations have the resources they need to continue saving lives for generations to come.”

“As a councilman and volunteer EMT of nearly 40 years, I understand personally how our nation’s EMS system needs support,” said Bridgewater Councilman Tim Ring. “This legislation that creates a grant program specifically for them is an important step forward in ensuring they have the funding they need to take care of our communities. I am deeply appreciative of Congressman Kean for always listening to his constituents, advocating on our behalf, and working to support emergency medical services and first responders across the country.”

In 2024, Congressman Kean’s bill, the Fire Grants and Safety Act, was signed into law. The Fire Grants and Safety Act provided a five-year reauthorization for the U.S. Fire Administration (USFA), the Assistance to Firefighter Grants (AFG) Program, and the Staffing for Adequate Fire and Emergency Response Grant (SAFER) Program.

Congressman Kean has secured nearly $22 million for first responders in New Jersey Seventh Congressional District through the Community Project Funding process.

title: CNMI Fishermen and Farmers eligible for USDA Diesel Fuel Relief Aid
text: The U.S. Department of Agriculture has announced $8 billion to provide one-time payments to fishermen and farmers to provide monetary relief from increased diesel fuel prices. CNMI fishermen and farmers, along with those from other U.S. territories, will be eligible to apply for relief under a special formula. To be considered, producers from the CNMI and other U.S. territories are encouraged to provide data on increased fuel costs to HarvestFuel@usda.gov, which they will then consider in determining reimbursement rates. Once those rates are determined, producers can then apply for cost reimbursement. Payment rates for their commodities will be set after USDA’s November payments for mainland staple crops.

title: FEMA Awards $279,000 for Emergency Power at Tinian Fire Station
text: Reliable emergency power is essential for emergency responders, especially when typhoons disrupt electricity across our islands. Through FEMA’s Hazard Mitigation Grant Program, Tinian Department of Fire and EMS Station #7 will receive $279,548 in federal funding, covering 100% of the project cost, to install a generator and above-ground fuel storage tank. Funded under FEMA’s disaster recovery efforts following Super Typhoon Yutu, this investment will help the station maintain critical operations during power outages and strengthen Tinian’s emergency response capabilities. Keeping our first responders equipped and ready is an important part of protecting our communities.

We were honored to visit and share about the programs our office offers to students such as Service Academy Nominations, Congressional Art Competition, Congressional App Challenge, and internships. title: More Than $1.3 Million in FEMA Funding for CUC Emergency Generator Support
text: The Commonwealth Utilities Corporation (CUC) has received $1,308,655.88 in federal funding to support emergency generator operations following Super Typhoon Sinlaku. This includes $1,059,132.68 for emergency protective measures and an additional $249,523.20 to fund the use of temporary generators to help maintain essential services and reduce immediate threats to public health, safety, and property. Both awards are funded at 100% by FEMA under Section 403 of the Stafford Act, with no local cost share required. Reliable power is critical to our communities, especially in the aftermath of a disaster, and this assistance helps CUC respond to urgent needs while supporting the Commonwealth’s recovery.

title: Responding to the Suspension of EVS-TAP
text: Last week, the Department of Homeland Security announced the suspension of the CNMI Economic Vitality and Security Travel Authorization Program (EVS-TAP), adding another challenge to an already struggling tourism industry. With visitor arrivals declining and our businesses and families facing increasing economic pressure, the consequences of a prolonged suspension could be significant. Immediately following the announcement, I spoke directly with the White House, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, and House leadership about the suspension and the urgency of restoring the program. Secretary Mullin personally assured me that he would work with the CNMI to understand and address the concerns that led to the decision. I also wrote to President Trump requesting his personal intervention and an expedited review involving DHS, the Department of the Interior, and the Commonwealth government. EVS-TAP was established during his first administration, and I believe there is a path to resolving the outstanding concerns and restoring the program. Already, I have spoken with senior leaders in both the administration and Congress about the critical condition of the CNMI economy and the role the federal government has in preventing its collapse. Our tourism industry, government revenues, and the livelihoods of our people are all connected, and federal decisions affecting our economy must take those consequences seriously. EVS-TAP remains suspended, and there are procedures for addressing the security and law enforcement concerns that may arise under the program. My immediate priority is working with our federal partners to resolve the outstanding issues and secure its resumption as quickly as possible. There is a great deal at stake for our Commonwealth, and I will continue pressing for the urgency our situation demands.

title: Rota Mayor’s Office Receives $320,000 in FEMA Funding for Equipment
text: Rota’s recovery efforts continue with $320,680 in FEMA funding approved for the Rota Mayor’s Office to purchase equipment under an alternate project following Typhoon Mawar. This $427,574 project is funded through FEMA’s Public Assistance Program under Section 406 of the Stafford Act, with the federal government covering 75% of the cost. This investment will help strengthen the Mayor’s Office’s resources and support its ability to serve the people of Rota.

title: Supporting Higher Education and Workforce Development
text: On Tuesday, we welcomed Northern Marianas College Interim President Frankie Eliptico and members of the State Higher Education Executive Officers Association (SHEEO), Christen Whitfield, Rob Andersen, and Tom Harnisch, to the Saipan district office. SHEEO advocates for state-level leadership in higher education policy and connects state higher education systems with the federal government. The organization has represented NMC’s interests for more than a decade. NMC was recently selected as one of only eight institutions nationwide to receive a highly competitive grant to help implement Workforce Pell programs, expanding opportunities for students to gain skills for in-demand careers. Congratulations to President Eliptico for your outstanding leadership and to the entire NMC team for your dedication to strengthening higher education opportunities and creating pathways to success for students across the Marianas.

title: VCU Students Study the CNMI’s Resilience and Recovery
text:
Virginia Commonwealth University (VCU), through its Institute for Sustainable Energy and Environment, brought students to Saipan, Tinian, and Guam to study how territorial governance, disaster recovery, and environmental challenges affect island communities. Working alongside students from the University of Guam, they explored issues ranging from typhoon recovery and clean energy to food security and deep-sea mining, with the goal of better understanding these challenges and informing future solutions. Having grown up in the CNMI, I know our islands are more than just a place on the map. They are home to resilient people who continue to rebuild after devastating storms, including Super Typhoons Sinlaku and Bavi. We’re glad to see these students come to Saipan and Tinian to listen to our people and see firsthand the realities our communities face. We hope their research brings greater attention to the CNMI’s needs and reminds more Americans that our islands have valuable lessons to share with the rest of our nation.
