title: Working with Navy Leadership on the CNMI’s Economic and Infrastructure Needs
text: The economic challenges facing our Commonwealth have become increasingly urgent, and I have been working to make sure our federal partners understand what is at stake for our people and for the United States' long-term presence in the Pacific. On Tuesday, I met with Admiral Mietus to discuss the worsening economic conditions in the CNMI, including the impact of declining tourism, rising utility costs, and the recent suspension of EVS-TAP. We talked about the need for a coordinated federal response and the importance of recognizing that a strong local economy is essential to supporting our nation's defense interests in the Marianas. The following day, we continued those conversations with Admiral Mietus and Andy Weedon, Director of Policy and Strategy for the Secretary of the Navy, alongside Governor Apatang. Our discussions focused on infrastructure investments that could benefit both our communities and the military, including improvements to our power systems, airports, and harbors on Saipan, Tinian, and Rota. We also discussed opportunities to move priority projects forward through federal infrastructure programs and the importance of keeping our agencies working together to turn these discussions into actual investments. I appreciate Admiral Mietus and Director Weedon taking the time to engage with us on these issues and see the challenges facing our islands firsthand. There is a great deal of work ahead, and I look forward to continuing these conversations as we pursue the federal support and investments our Commonwealth needs.

title: Liccardo Joins San José Community Leaders to Urge Voters to Cast Their Ballots
text:
SAN JOSÉ, CA – Today, Congressman Sam Liccardo (CA-16), joined the Amigos de Guadalupe Center for Justice and Empowerment and local community leaders at Mexican Heritage Plaza in East San José to encourage eligible voters to cast their ballots ahead of tomorrow’s election. The press conference came amid heightened concerns about immigration enforcement activity in Santa Clara County and federal efforts to obtain confidential voter information.

“We have thousands of volunteers throughout the country and thousands of lawyers ready to run to court as soon as there is a violation. So far, the courts have consistently been with us, whether on mail-in voting or attempts to access voter rolls. We will continue to fight these battles on the streets and in the courts. So I ask everyone: Please participate. Please vote. We are working together to ensure your vote counts," said Liccardo.

Liccardo also reminded voters that it is not too late to participate in tomorrow’s election. Voters can return their ballots to an official drop box or vote center before 8 p.m. on Tuesday, November 3. Eligible voters who have not yet registered can also register and vote at a county vote center through Election Day.

title: Lofgren Secures Over $54 Million for Pajaro River Flood Protection As El Niño Is Expected to Strengthen
text:
WATSONVILLE, CA — Today, Congresswoman Zoe Lofgren (CA-18) delivered a $54,830,000 check for the Pajaro River Flood Risk Management Project, one of her 13 community projects she submitted for the Fiscal Year 2026 congressional appropriations cycle. This is the largest single community project that Lofgren secured this year, which is being completed by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) San Francisco District, in partnership with the Pajaro Regional Flood Management Agency (PRFMA). Senators Alex Padilla (D-CA) and Adam Schiff (D-CA) also requested congressional funding for this project.

“With El Niño expected to intensify in the early months of 2027, it’s critical that the residents and businesses along the Pajaro River have necessary flood protection,” said Rep. Lofgren. “Last year, I was proud to announce nearly $40 million for levee and floodwall construction in Watsonville, and I’m proud to have submitted this additional $54 million as one of my community projects this year. That’s going to help save lives and property, and I’m proud to have worked with Senators Padilla and Schiff to prioritize this project funding.”

“Consistent funding for the Pajaro River flood control project is critically important, and we are grateful to Rep. Lofgren for her work to keep the project moving forward and fulfilling our commitments to the vulnerable residents and businesses in the Pajaro Valley,” said Mark Strudley, Executive Director of PRFMA.

“Future improvements to the levee will make a real difference in reducing flood risks and protecting the people who call Watsonville and the Pajaro Valley home,” said Watsonville City Manager Tamara Vides. This is an investment in the safety, stability, and future of our community. We are thankful for the advocacy and support provided by Congresswoman Lofgren.”

The residents and businesses of Watsonville and Pajaro have been waiting for 50 years for flood protection and during that time have suffered significant damage and loss of life due to weather events. On March 11, 2023, a serious levee failure resulted in the evacuation of more than 2,000 people in the Town of Pajaro, 200 water rescues, significant flooding of farms, and closure of Highway 1. The farms impacted by flooding are vital contributors to the regional agricultural industry, where none of the fruit and vegetable crops are federally subsidized and floods can result in the loss of 2-3 growing seasons.

According to the National Weather Service, El Niño continues to strengthen with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027. Lofgren has urged Californians to prepare for storm season and sign up for emergency alerts. Tips and resources for El Niño can be viewed on her website.

title: Rep. Miller Announced $4.5 Million for Rural Water Infrastructure Expansion Benefiting Seven Illinois Counties
text:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Mary Miller (IL-15) announced $4.5 million in federal funding to support the expansion of EJ Water Cooperative’s Delbert Mundt Water Treatment Plant. The investment will double the facility’s treatment capacity, strengthening access to reliable water service for families, farmers, and businesses across seven Central Illinois counties: Shelby, Effingham, Montgomery, Fayette, Cumberland, Christian, and Clay.

“Our farmers, small businesses, and rural communities are the backbone of America, and they deserve the infrastructure necessary to thrive. I’m proud to have secured $4.5 million to support this critical expansion in Illinois’ 15th District,” said Congresswoman Mary Miller. “This investment will meet growing demand and strengthen the essential infrastructure that families and businesses across our rural communities will depend on for generations.”

Background:

Founded in 1989, EJ Water Cooperative is the largest rural water cooperative in Illinois, serving a rural population of more than 48,000 residents. The Delbert Mundt Water Treatment Plant was constructed in 2010 near Beecher City and serves EJ Water’s fastest-growing western service area.

As demand continues to increase, EJ Water has expanded its infrastructure to support rural communities, including the construction of a 250-million-gallon reservoir in 2023. The cooperative also works with smaller municipalities facing aging or inadequate water treatment facilities, helping provide dependable, affordable water service to underserved communities throughout Central Illinois.

title: Congressman Menefee Joins the Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus
text:
HOUSTON, TX — Representative Christian D. Menefee (TX-18) has joined the Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus (CAPAC) as an Associate Member, bringing the Caucus to a historic 86 Members of the U.S. House of Representatives and Senate, its largest membership since its founding.

“Houston is one of the most diverse cities in the nation. The strength and resilience of our many cultures, including our Asian American, Native Hawaiian, and Pacific Islander communities, are woven into the fabric of our district. I’m proud to join the Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus. More than 40,000 AANHPI residents call TX-18 home, and I’m committed to making sure our community has a seat at the table. Thank you to Chair Meng for the warm welcome. I look forward to being an ally in this fight,” said Rep. Christian D. Menefee.

“I am thrilled to welcome Congressman Christian Menefee as CAPAC’s new Associate Member,” said Rep. Grace Meng, Chair of the Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus. “We need allies in Congress who are committed to fighting for the needs of Asian Americans, Native Hawaiians, and Pacific Islanders across the country—including right in the heart of Houston. Rep. Menefee will be a strong advocate for our communities, and we are proud to have him as the newest member of our ever-growing caucus.”

Founded in 1994, the bicameral Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus is composed of 86 Members of Congress who advocate on behalf of Asian American, Native Hawaiian, and Pacific Islander communities. The Caucus is led by Congresswoman Grace Meng, who was elected CAPAC Chair in 2024.

In response to this grant notice, U.S. Congressman Morgan Griffith (R-VA) issued the following statement:

“Improved broadband networks strengthen rural community access to remote learning, telemedicine and telework.

“This grant for more than $2.4 million helps iGo install new broadband infrastructure to serve internet to Dickenson County households.”

BACKGROUND

According to USDA Rural Development, this project is estimated to benefit more than 300 people in Dickenson County, including 14 businesses and two farms.

As part of the project, iGo will establish a community center in Haysi for resident to use free high-speed internet.

title: Rep. Obernolte Demands Answers on Medi-Cal Oversight
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. Congressman Jay Obernolte (CA-23) led members of the California delegation in sending a letter to California Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) Director Michelle Baass expressing concerns over the department's oversight of the Medi-Cal program following a recent report from the California State Auditor identifying deficiencies in its efforts to investigate potentially improper billing and recover overpayments.

The letter, signed by Representatives Ken Calvert (CA-41), Tom McClintock (CA-05), David Valadao (CA-22), Young Kim (CA-40), Vince Fong (CA-20), and James Gallagher (CA-01), requests information on the department's efforts to strengthen program oversight, address potentially fraudulent billing, and safeguard taxpayer dollars.

According to the October 15 audit, DHCS identified approximately 28,000 Medi-Cal providers as high risk for potentially improper billing during fiscal year 2024–2025, but had not initiated referrals or investigations for more than 26,000 of them. These providers collectively accounted for at least $12 billion in Medi-Cal services during that period.

The audit also found that DHCS identified more than $2 billion in provider overpayments between fiscal years 2020 and 2025, approximately $300 million of which remain unrecovered.

The findings come amid additional federal scrutiny of California's Medi-Cal program. On October 20, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) announced it would defer an additional $1.2 billion in federal Medicaid payments to California over concerns regarding documentation supporting certain Medi-Cal expenditures.

“Medi-Cal provides critical care to millions of Californians, and every dollar lost to fraud is a dollar that is not available to help our most vulnerable citizens access the care they need,” said Congressman Jay Obernolte (CA-23). “The California State Auditor's findings raise serious concerns about the state's oversight of this program, particularly the failure to investigate more than 26,000 providers identified as high risk for potentially improper billing. California taxpayers deserve to know that their money is being used wisely and appropriately. Stronger oversight is necessary to prevent fraud, waste, and abuse while protecting the patients who depend on this critical program.”

“It’s critical that California take every measure possible to eliminate fraud in the Medi-Cal program. We owe it taxpayers to verify payments to Medi-Cal providers and ensure all of our resources are being dedicated to the actual health care needs of Californians,” said Congressman Ken Calvert (CA-41).

“California’s Medi-Cal program is a critical lifeline for our most vulnerable, and every dollar lost to fraud is a dollar that can’t go toward helping those in need,” said Congressman David Valadao (CA-22). “The California Department of Health Care Services has a responsibility to properly investigate fraudulent billing and improper payments, and I urge the agency to take immediate action to strengthen program oversight, hold bad actors accountable, and ensure taxpayer funds are being used appropriately.”

“Medi-Cal is supposed to be a lifeline for California’s most vulnerable, not an opportunity for fraudsters to cash in at taxpayers’ expense,” said Congresswoman Young Kim (CA-40). “The fact that California failed to investigate thousands of providers flagged for potential fraud, despite those providers accounting for $12 billion in claims, raises serious questions about the state’s oversight efforts. Every dollar lost to fraud is a dollar that could have gone toward caring for seniors, mothers, and children who depend on the services Medi-Cal provides. Californians deserve answers, accountability, and assurance that their tax dollars are going where they’re needed most.”

title: Rep. Panetta Announces Over $3.8 Million for Santa Cruz  Fire Department Medical Response Vehicle Pilot Program
text:
Santa Cruz, CA – United States Representative Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) announced $3,837,779 in federal funding for the Santa Cruz Fire Department to test a faster, more targeted response to medical emergencies, including traffic crashes. The funding comes from the Safe Streets and Roads for All (SS4A) grant program, which helps improve roadway safety by investing in safety strategies to reduce serious traffic injuries and fatalities.

The project combines two tools to help improve emergency response on Santa Cruz roadways. It will test a cloud-based system that gives emergency vehicles priority at traffic signals, connected to the dispatch system, as well as a smaller medical response vehicle for calls that do not involve a fire, including traffic crashes. The City of Santa Cruz will evaluate whether these tools improve response times and care after crashes, particularly along roads with high rates of serious injuries and key routes to hospitals.

“Every second counts for first responders when it comes to driving on our local roads and highways,” said Rep. Panetta. “This federal investment will allow the city of Santa Cruz to test potentially lifesaving technology to help emergency vehicles reach people more quickly and first responders provide timely, effective care. I’m proud to ensure that the federal government plays its part to help our local first responders do their job for the safety of communities in California’s 19th Congressional District.”

“This grant will allow Santa Cruz to explore new ways to help first responders reach injured patients faster, provide lifesaving care, and improve roadway safety,” said Santa Cruz Mayor Fred Keeley. “I am grateful for Congressman Panetta’s support in delivering this significant federal investment to strengthen emergency response and make our community safer.”

“Keeping our community safe is one of our most important responsibilities, and this investment gives Santa Cruz an exciting opportunity to strengthen how we respond to emergencies. We’re grateful to Congressman Panetta for securing this funding and recognizing the importance of investing in innovative solutions that can help save lives and make our streets safer for everyone. We’re excited to test these tools, evaluate their effectiveness, and identify opportunities to improve service to our community,” said Santa Cruz City Manager Matt Huffaker.

The SS4A grant program was established by the bipartisan Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act in 2021. Since the program’s inception, the cities of Santa Cruz, Monterey, Paso Robles, and San Jose, together with Santa Cruz County, Santa Clara County, the Transportation Agency for Monterey County, and the San Luis Obispo Council of Governments, have received more than $28.7 million through the SS4A program.

Rep. Panetta has previously secured federal investments for a new fire engine in Santa Cruz, pedestrian safety and lighting improvements along Bay Avenue in Capitola, and road safety improvements along Highways 9 and 236 in Boulder Creek.

title: From Texas Scorecard: Chip Roy Seeks DOJ Review of Allegations Surrounding Travis County DA’s Refusal To Prosecute Afghan National
text:
The below story appeared in the Texas Scorecard:

U.S. Reps. Chip Roy and Josh Brecheen are seeking records from the U.S. Department of Justice and an investigation into whistleblower allegations involving Travis County District Attorney José Garza’s decision not to prosecute an Afghan national accused of felony solicitation of prostitution.

The lawmakers’ letter cites a September 14 whistleblower complaint from Major Joshua Mast concerning Afghan national Aminullah Amin. According to the lawmakers, Garza’s office declined to prosecute the solicitation charges on July 22, citing the “interest of justice.”

Amin is embroiled in a custody dispute with Mast and his wife over a seven-year-old girl.

“The complaint raises the question whether the charging decision may have been improperly influenced so that the accused in that case could continue his custody pursuit of [the] seven-year-old little girl in our nation’s highest court,” the congressmen wrote.

The custody dispute began after an Afghan baby was found in the rubble of a rural compound raided by U.S. Army Rangers.

The State Department helped place her with an Afghan couple identified as relatives, who raised her for 18 months while Joshua Mast and his wife obtained a Virginia adoption order without notifying them.

After helping the Afghan family evacuate to the United States in 2021, Mast took custody of the girl. Lower Virginia courts ruled in the Afghan couple’s favor, but the state’s highest court sided with the Masts, citing a six-month statutory deadline for challenging the adoption.

The U.S. Supreme Court declined to hear the Afghan couple’s appeal earlier this month.

Roy (R–Austin) and Brecheen (R–OK) also request a review of evidence from two 2021 forensic extractions of phones used by Amin. The lawmakers say Mast’s complaint identifies potential investigative leads involving national security and immigration screening.

“The Complaint identifies leads involving alleged Taliban contacts, possible al-Qaeda connections, and eleven distinct SIM-card identifiers associated with one of the phones,” they wrote.

This letter follows a June committee inquiry into Garza’s immigration-related policies.

Roy, along with U.S. Reps. Jim Jordan (R–OH) and Tom McClintock (R–CA), wrote to Garza earlier this year “concerning his office’s immigration-related policies and their consequences for public safety and the rule of law.”

“Under your leadership, the Travis County District Attorney’s Office has routinely undermined the rule of law under the guise of safeguarding the public,” the congressmen wrote. “You previously committed to ‘[p]rotect immigrant communities’ by ‘creat[ing] a [district attorney’s] office that considers the impact of charges and convictions’ on foreign nationals and ‘ensures that the sentence imposed is not unduly harsh for any class of people.’”

Roy and Brecheen raised concerns that Garza is continuing a “soft-on-crime” approach that could also threaten national security.

“Shielding criminal aliens from immigration enforcement in Travis County or elsewhere undermines public safety and impedes enforcement of federal law,” Roy and Brecheen wrote.

“Above all, unresolved questions about potential terrorism connections involving a foreign national arrested for an apparent felony and pursuing custody of a child in American courts demand prompt examination.”

Garza has not responded to a request for comment regarding Roy and Brecheen’s accusations against him.

title: Salinas, Bonamici, Merkley, Wyden Secure over $500,000 for Tualatin Soil and Water Conservation District
text:
Tualatin, OR — Today, Congresswomen Andrea Salinas (OR-06) and Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), alongside Oregon Senators Ron Wyden and Jeff Merkley, announced they secured the release of over $530,000 in federal funding from the Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS) to support Tualatin Soil and Water Conservation District (TSWCD).

In 2022, TSWCD applied to the NRCS for funding to improve fish habitat in Washington County. This work included replacing deteriorated culverts with bridges and modern culverts that help threatened species like steelhead trout move through local waterways. In February 2024, NRCS approved and obligated $1,074,887 to reimburse TSWCD for their work.

As of early September 2026, NRCS had only paid $543,837 of the over $1.07 million they had promised to TSWCD. This $531,000 shortfall has severely challenged TSWCD’s budget and would have stuck the taxpayers of Washington County with the bill. Following outreach from the Oregon delegation, NRSC honored its commitment and released the final sum to TSWCD.

“When Oregonians make a promise, we keep it. The federal government should be held to the same standard,” said Rep. Salinas. “Tualatin Soil and Water did the work to improve our waterways, and Washington County taxpayers should never have been left holding the bag. I’m glad we got this money out the door and where it belongs.”

“Supporting threatened species and their habitats reflects Oregon values and our commitment to environmental protection, and I was grateful when the Tualatin Soil and Water Conservation District secured federal funds to improve fish habitat in Washington County,” said Rep. Bonamici. “Unfortunately, the Trump administration paid only about half of the promised funding, leaving Washington County taxpayers to pick up the balance. I’m glad that my colleagues and I were able to help resolve this issue and secure all the funds the water conservation district needed for the project."

“Thanks to our efforts, this funding is finally moving forward and will help ensure the Tualatin Soil and Water Conservation District can continue its work to improve waterways in Washington County,” said Sen. Merkley.“Oregon’s native fish are the lifeblood of our state, supporting the health and vitality of our communities, local economies, and Tribes who have been here since time immemorial. I’ll keep pushing to secure the necessary federal funds to protect our state’s ecosystems for generations to come.”

“I’m glad the full-court press by the delegation unlocked these resources promised by the federal government to the Tualatin Soil and Water Conservation District,” Wyden said. “These funds will keep waterways improvements on track, helping with water quality and fish habitat alike in Washington County.”

“The Tualatin Soil and Water Conservation District much appreciates Congresswoman Salinas and her staff for their work in helping the District receive payment from the U.S. Department of Agriculture for a successful fish habitat project in the Gales Creek watershed of Washington County,” said Dean P. Moberg, Tualatin Soil and Water Conservation District Treasurer. “We were impressed with the staff's quick understanding of the payment problem we faced, and we are grateful for the Congresswoman's exceptional response. The letter Congresswoman Salinas provided, along with Congresswoman Bonamici and Senators Merkley and Wyden, was surely instrumental in cutting through red tape and securing the payment of over one half million dollars in federal assistance that had been held up for this project. This payment will greatly facilitate the Tualatin Soil and Water Conservation District's work in helping residents of Washington County conserve natural resources with voluntary and locally led projects.

title: Peters Urges Trump Admin to Cancel Mass Deportation Flights to Afghanistan and Iran
text:
San Diego, CA. — Today, U.S. Representative Scott Peters (CA-50) led 65 bicameral Members of Congress on a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin, demanding the immediate cancellation of any deportation flights carrying Afghans and Iranians, whether sent directly or through another country.

This letter comes after reports that over 150 Afghans could be deported to Pakistan in the coming days, which would constitute one of the largest single expulsions of Afghans ever. San Diego has served as a primary hub for incoming Afghan refugees, with nearly 5,000 resettling in the region. The Members also expressed concern over another flight with a mass deportation of Iranians — the first since the U.S. launched its military conflict against Iran— and that relatives of Afghans who helped American troops could be among those on board.

“Our nation made a promise to stand by Afghans who risked their lives and their families’ safety to stand by U.S. service members,” the Members wrote, adding that deporting them “is a violation of that promise and our moral obligations to the Afghan community who stood alongside our troops.”

The Members emphasized the well-documented danger awaiting deportees. The State Department lists Afghanistan as a Level 4 “Do Not Travel” country, and for those who aided U.S. forces, “their assistance to U.S. troops puts a target on these individuals and their families to this day.” They detail the torture, detention, and extrajudicial killing of dissidents and LGBTQ persons, as well as the severe repression of women — noting that women and LGBTQ refugees could be on the flight.

The Members also raised alarm over reports that Iranians, including women, Christian converts, and pro-democracy activists, may be deported to Iran, where they face imprisonment, torture, and a possible death sentence. “Sending people who sought protection from the Islamic Republic of Iran back to a war zone and a repressive regime is unconscionable,” they wrote. They cited how even President Trump has warned about the dangers faced by pro-democracy and anti-government protesters in Iran.

The Members stressed that routing a flight through a third country does not change U.S. obligations, and urged the Trump Administration to warn Pakistan that the U.S. will not accept its participation in sending deportees onward to the Taliban.

These individuals “came to the U.S. because they believed in its promise of democracy, religious freedom, and liberty,” the Members concluded, and “we must uphold those values and commitments, not abandon people to autocratic regimes.”

“Sixty-six members of Congress, from both chambers, needed less than 24 hours to say what every veteran of the Afghanistan war already knows: you don’t hand the people who stood with our troops to the Taliban. When even the Taliban are voicing ‘serious concern’ about your deportation plan, you’ve lost the moral argument and the national security one. This flight isn’t immigration enforcement. It’s a betrayal with a boarding pass, and the whole world is watching whether America keeps its word. We are grateful to Rep. Peters for leading. Secretary Rubio and Secretary Mullin, ground this plane,” said Shawn VanDiver, U.S. Navy veteran and President and Founder of #AfghanEvac.

"Having effectively dismantled our protection system, this administration is set to deport vulnerable people back to Afghanistan and Iran, in violation of our human rights commitments and our nation's values," said Sarah Mehta, deputy director of immigration policy at the ACLU. "So many of these men and women never had a meaningful opportunity to defend their claims and are now the casualties of this administration's assault on asylum. We thank Congressman Peters for his leadership and all the members standing against these unconscionable deportations back to persecution, torture, or even death."

The Members requested an immediate response. Read the full letter here.

Background:

San Diego has served as a primary hub for incoming Afghan refugees, and Rep. Peters has been a staunch advocate for the safe relocation, protection, and legal adjustment of Afghan wartime allies who served alongside U.S. forces. He is a cosponsor of the Enduring Welcome Act to codify the Office of the Coordinator for Afghan Relocation Efforts (CARE) within the State Department, and the Afghan Adjustment Act to help settle Afghans and their families who supported U.S. forces.

In September, Rep. Peters led a Congressional delegation on a letter to the Trump Administration urging them to reunite the families of U.S. service members with their loved ones stranded overseas, and to reconnect Afghans with immediate family already lawfully in the U.S. In July, he hosted a virtual town hall with Afghan allies stranded at the Camp As Sayliyah facility in Doha. And in February, Rep. Peters attended a shadow hearing where he highlighted the consequences of the Trump administration's decisions to freeze the U.S. refugee admissions program and eliminate Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Afghans.

title: Reps Peters, Vargas, Levin, and Jacobs Back San Diego County Registrar of Voters Amid Trump Admin Probe for Voter Data
text:
San Diego, CA — Today, U.S. Representative Scott Peters (CA-50) led members of the San Diego Congressional delegation, Reps. Juan Vargas (CA-52), Mike Levin (CA-49), and Sara Jacobs (CA-51), in a letter to U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche amid the Department of Justice’s (DOJ) attempt to sanction voter rolls across California, including in San Diego County’s Registrars of Voters (ROV).

The DOJ demanded that San Diego’s ROV provide voter information for over 1,700 voters, including driver’s license numbers, Social Security numbers, and voter registration applications, within 48 hours, and withhold their ballots until their citizenship is confirmed. In its response, the County pushed back against several unsubstantiated claims and argued that the DOJ's probe violated several election laws.

The Members' letter reinforced the County’s claims and acknowledged that California’s registrars follow all state and federal election laws, including citizenship attestation and database verification through the California Secretary of State. They argued that the DOJ’s letter cites no legal authority to direct county ballot administration and that it violates the National Voter Registration Act’s (NVRA) 90-day quiet period against systematically removing voters from the rolls.

“The information requested by DOJ is intended to confirm the department’s unsubstantiated allegations of noncitizen voting in California,” the Members noted, also pointing to the data cited by DOJ, which the Agency itself conceded “may be outdated or incomplete.”

The Members also stated that unverified fraud allegations do not give registrars authority to violate federal law by refusing to count the votes of people already deemed eligible. They added that the DOJ’s demand fails to explain who would determine citizenship status, how, or when, less than a week before Election Day.

“The request from DOJ violates the NVRA, Voting Rights Act, California state law, and jeopardizes Californians’ constitutional right to vote,” the Members concluded, adding that “as Members of the California Congressional delegation, we commend the work of our state ROVs to ensure state and federal election laws are upheld.”

title: Rep. Summer Lee, House Labor Leaders Demand Answers Over Corporate Union-Busting, Enforcement of Federal Transparency Laws
text:
Full Letter Text

PITTSBURGH, PA – NOVEMBER 2, 2026 — Today, Congresswoman Summer L. Lee (PA-12) joined House Education and Workforce Committee Ranking Member Robert C. “Bobby” Scott (VA-03) and Subcommittee on Health, Employment, Labor, and Pensions Ranking Member Mark DeSaulnier (CA-10) in demanding answers from the Trump Administration over its failure to adequately enforce federal transparency laws governing corporations and union-busting consultants.

In aletter to Office of Labor-Management Standards (OLMS) Director Elisabeth Messenger, the lawmakers raised serious concerns about widespread failures by employers and anti-union consultants to disclose how much money they spend attempting to influence workers' decisions to organize.

Too often, when workers exercise their right to organize a union, corporations and bosses hire outside consultants to wage anti-union campaigns. Over the last several decades, union-avoidance has become a multi-billion-dollar industry. The latest analysis found that companies spend approximately $1.7 billion every year, including nearly $500 million on union-busting consultants, to break their organizing drives. Some consultants are reportedly paid $500 per hour or $4,000 per day for their services.

Under the Labor-Management Reporting and Disclosure Act (LMRDA), employers and consultants are required to file public reports about their matter because it allows workers to see how much their bosses are spending to influence their decision to unionize. However, for decades, employers and union-busting consultants have routinely failed to meet this requirement, allowing bosses and their consultants to operate in the shadows. Under the Trump Administration, the problem is only becoming worse. A recent watchdog report found that, as of August 8, 2026, nearly 60 percent of employers required to file a disclosure in 2025 have still not submitted their reports—the largest year-over-year decline on record.

“Over the last several years, while worker organizing has skyrocketed, employers have increasingly responded with hostile anti-union campaigns, including by hiring well-compensated outside consultants. As more employers seek to quash their workers’ unionization drives, it is imperative that employer and consultant disclosure requirements under the LMRDA are robustly enforced by OLMS, so workers have a complete picture of who is attempting to influence their decision as they exercise their right to organize,” wrote the Members.

To determine whether OLMS is effectively carrying out its responsibility to enforce the LMRDA, the Members requested a response to their extensive questions by no later than November 16, 2026.

title: Womack Joins Senator Boozman in Welcoming Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle to Arkansas’s Third District
text:
ARKANSAS—November 2, 2026…Congressman Steve Womack (AR-3) joined Senator John Boozman (AR) in welcoming Acting Secretary of the Army Adam Telle to Arkansas’s Third District. Acting Secretary Telle’s visit was part of a series of meetings, tours, and roundtables across the state highlighting Arkansas’s national security contributions and future opportunities to partner with academic institutions and the private sector to enhance solutions to the Army’s logistics, supply chain, and technological needs.

Congressman Steve Womack said, “It was a privilege to have Acting Secretary of the Army Adam Telle in Arkansas’s Third District to showcase how our region is contributing to the state’s reputation as a major U.S. defense hub. From conducting groundbreaking research to being the home of leading logistics experts, Northwest Arkansas—especially with the help of our university partners—is making strides to provide the solutions that strengthen our national security and give our warfighters a competitive edge against adversaries."

Senator John Boozman said, “It was a pleasure to host Acting Army Secretary Telle in Arkansas and showcase the important role our state plays in strengthening our nation’s defense. From the dedicated workforce at Pine Bluff Arsenal to Walmart’s expertise in supply chain logistics and the innovative research taking place at the University of Arkansas, these visits highlighted the talent, resources and capabilities unique to Arkansas. Our delegation is grateful for the chance to showcase these strengths and we look forward to continuing to build on them to support the Army and other national security needs.”

Acting Secretary Adam Telle said, “From the vital production lines at Pine Bluff, to the global distribution engine of Walmart, to the world-class logistics and materials research at the University of Arkansas, this visit demonstrated the total national ecosystem required to secure our nation. By uniting military capability, private enterprise, and academic innovation, we guarantee the American Soldier is never in a fair fight.” Acting Secretary Telle continued, “The forward momentum we saw across Arkansas wouldn't be possible without the leadership and advocacy of President Trump, Secretary of War Hegseth, Senator Boozman, Senator Cotton, Congressman Womack and the entire Arkansas delegation. They are backing our warfighters with the resourcing and legislative firepower needed to modernize our organic industrial base and supercharge our installations. That’s how we empower our Soldiers with every competitive advantage when they step onto the battlefield.”

Alongside Senator Boozman and Congressman Womack, Acting Secretary Telle visited Walmart’s Global Security Operations Center (GSOC). Staffed 24/7, the GSOC identifies and tracks events that could disrupt supply chains around the world and can be a key partner in our national emergency response when disaster strikes.

At the University of Arkansas, Acting Secretary Telle, Senator Boozman, and Congressman Womack saw firsthand how students, researchers, and experts are working to equip our warfighters with cutting-edge technology to protect our nation.

With the leaders of the Army, University of Arkansas, and Contested Logistics Consortium at the Sam M. Walton College of Business, Secretary Telle, Senator Boozman, and Congressman Womack discussed how Northwest Arkansas’s supply chain expertise can assist the military in navigating complex operational environments.

At the Grady E. Harvell Civil Engineering Research and Education Center (CEREC), Dr. Micah Hale and Assistant Professor Morgan Broberg provided Secretary Telle and Congressman Womack an up close look at the innovative ways they are tackling commercial and military infrastructure deployment challenges.

title: Fetterman Statement in Support of Coca-Cola Teamsters Local 110 Strike
text:
BRADDOCK, PA — In announcing his support for the Teamsters Union Local 110 members who are on strike at the Abarta Coca Cola Plants in Cambria and Clearfield Counties, U.S. Senator John Fetterman (D-PA) today released the following statement:

“I’m proud to stand with the Teamsters Local 110 and every union member fighting for fair wages and a safe workplace. I urge Abarta Coca-Cola management to come back to the table and work together to create a fair deal for everyone.”

“The company did not want to bargain in good faith, we gave them several proposals and they simply said no and left. We filed a ULP. They would not counter. We tried to tell them what it would take to get it passed and they said we will not reward the behavior of striking. They now said they will not come back to the table till January of 2027 they will just hire replacements because sales are up 6% and they will be fine. These members are the lowest paid and pay the highest amount in health care in comparison to Greensburg and Houston facilities,” said Darrell Watt, President of Teamsters Local 110.

Teamsters Local 110 have been in negotiations with Abarta Coca-Cola since July and have been on strike for 10 days. The union members have rejected two contract proposals due to concerns over increases in healthcare costs and unfair wages. As of now, Local 110 leadership are waiting for Abarta Coca-Cola to return to the table and continue negotiations.
